name: Grid Pathfinder
description: Finds a route between two tiles that the agent asking for it can actually walk, which means honouring its climb limits rather than only its footprint. movement.pathfinding_system is the continuous-space answer and depends on world.terrain_generator; this one depends on world.tile_grid and on the agent, because on stepped ground the question 'is there a path' has no answer until you say who is walking. Two agents with different maxStepUp get different routes across the same map, and one of them may get none.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application (generator/iso/GridPath.ts); not verifiable from this repository.
The 3D runtime has no tile graph to search.

inputs.name: diagonalCost
inputs.description: Cost of a diagonal step relative to 1 for a straight one. It is not a look-and-feel knob: a search that allows diagonals must use a heuristic that admits them, and pairing diagonal movement with a Manhattan heuristic overestimates the remaining distance and quietly returns routes that are not the shortest.

inputs.name: cutCorners
inputs.description: Whether a diagonal step may pass between two blocked tiles. False is the answer that matches what a player expects to be able to do.

inputs.name: climbCostPerLevel
inputs.description: Extra cost per level of elevation change. Zero makes hills free and routes go straight over them; large values make agents walk around.

inputs.name: maxExpandedNodes
inputs.description: A bound on the search, so an unreachable destination on a large map fails in bounded time rather than expanding every tile.
